context: Widen SNAPSHOT_TABLES to include findings, finding_evidence, finding_links, finding_events and finding_sections, and update RESTORE_LEGACY_REQUIRED_TABLES to match the importer's new contract - build_snapshot fails closed when they diverge, so both must move together. Do NOT touch EXPORT_TABLE_ALLOWLIST: the committed export must stay findings-free, and test_todo_db_export_allowlist.py enforces that. The snapshot is safe to widen because write_snapshot already refuses any destination inside a Git work tree, so prose cannot reach the repository. Add a test that a snapshot carries findings while a committed export still does not - the two boundaries must not drift into each other.
description: BenchBox half of Joe's 2026-07-30 option-A decision (carry findings across the todo-db migration). PR #1354 deliberately scoped the migration snapshot to SNAPSHOT_TABLES = frozenset(TRANSFER_TABLES) | {meta}, which excludes the findings domain, because restore-legacy discarded unknown tables anyway and shipping review prose that will be thrown away only risks leaking it. Once the todo-db side lands (restore-legacy-carry-findings-and-reject-unknown-tables, in the todo-db project), that reasoning inverts: findings must be IN the snapshot or the migration is still lossy. Ordering matters - widening the snapshot first would make it fail against today's importer once that importer starts rejecting unknown tables, which is part of the same todo-db item.

preserves.behavior: the committed export stays findings-free (EXPORT_TABLE_ALLOWLIST unchanged, test_todo_db_export_allowlist.py still passes)
write_snapshot keeps refusing destinations inside a Git work tree
